The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: The shop stopped confidently categorising many shoppers' purchases
Why, in plain words: Switching the shop to a newer model for sorting purchases into categories likely left capitalised words in product titles unrecognised: the new model only knows lowercase words, and the shop passed titles on without lowercasing them.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 7m 0s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #567 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
The shop stopped confidently categorising many shoppers' purchases while categoriser.model was v2
Incident: CategorisationConfidenceLow on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 02:05 to 02:12 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 02:16:40 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 02:11:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 02:05 UTC and was back to normal at 02:12 UTC, 7 minutes later. What its alert watches went from 90% before it began to 37.7% at its worst. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. Switching the shop to a newer model for sorting purchases into categories likely left capitalised words in product titles unrecognised: the new model only knows lowercase words, and the shop passed titles on without lowercasing them. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #567, for a person to review and merge. It was written against main, which does not contain the revision that ran: merged, it changes what runs only once a deploy carries it. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). If automatic sync is turned back on, or the service is deployed again, while the repository still sets the categoriser to v2, the new model could come back and many purchases could again be filed without a confident category.

Impact
7m 0s - onset until back to normal
0.9% to 1.4% - error rate, before onset and while broken on average (no rise)
90% to 45.5% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (worst minute 37.7%; the rule's line is 80%)
none - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
Model v2 looks words up exactly as it is given them, against a vocabulary built from titles that were already lowercased. The shop's `categorise` passes `title.split()` to `predict` without lowercasing it, a step v1 does itself inside `predict`. Under v2, any capitalised word in a purchase title missed the vocabulary, so the purchase was filed under "General" with `confident=False`. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Many shoppers' purchases were no longer filed confidently under a category, while failed requests stayed within their normal variation.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Share of purchases categorised confidently below 80% for 5m
    T5 02:11:06 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:05
why 1 The production categoriser had been switched from model v1 to model v2. Deploy P2 at 02:05:10 UTC changed categoriser.model in deploy/values-production.yaml from v1 to v2. That is the only file the diff D1 lists, and S1 shows v2 set at the running revision. As of 02:11:10 UTC, all 3 replicas ran that revision, and rolling the service back off it put things right (M1).
  Evidence:
    P2 02:05:10 UTC deploy 7c3ca00 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 7c3ca00 to io-shop, compared against d268103 - the revision deployed before it.
    S1 deploy/values-production.yaml at 7c3ca00
    T9 02:11:10 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 7c3ca00, deployed at 02:05:10
    M1 02:11:21 Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1: confirmed, still in place
    T18 02:14 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy P1 of revision d268103. The metrics read reach back before it and show the service healthy until the onset at 02:05 UTC, and rolling back to that revision was confirmed to bring the service back to normal.
      T4 02:11:05 Investigator Agent: Read back 361 minutes of metrics
      T5
      M1
      T18
    A flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 02:06; the Investigator Agent read back 2 production changes. A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:11:21.
      T7
      T8
      T13
why 2 With v2 loaded (S1), purchase titles with capitalised words likely stopped matching the model's lowercase vocabulary, so those purchases fell to the general category without a confident filing.
  Evidence:
    S1
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that runs a new categoriser model against mixed-case purchase titles and compares its confident share with the current model's before the config change ships. According to Code-Fix, the existing v2 tests used only words that were already lowercase. (AI-4)
- The model switch went out as a plain config change to the whole deployment. No staged rollout and no gate on the confidence series were seen. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The deployment at 02:05:10 UTC moved the categoriser from model v1 to v2 in deploy/values-production.yaml. Categorisation confidence fell from about 0.90 to about 0.40, while error rate, latency, memory and CPU stayed at baseline. The new model answers worse, but requests are not failing or slowing. | 0.60 | confirmed
C2 | The deployment changed a configuration value, categoriser.model, to v2 and the source code is untouched. This is the same change as the first explanation, read as a broken configuration value. | 0.25 | confirmed, as tested for C1

Trigger
categoriser.model went from v1 to v2 at 02:05:10 UTC, in the deploy of 7c3ca00 that kuki started.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:11:21 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
 | 02:15 | Proposed a fix: PR #567 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:05 UTC. CategorisationConfidenceLow fired at 02:11 UTC, 6 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Share of purchases categorised confidently below 80% for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #567 | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a pre-release check for categoriser model changes: run the candidate model over a sample of real, mixed-case purchase titles and block the change if its confident share falls below the current model's. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Roll out categoriser model changes to part of the replicas first, and go on only if the confident-categorisation share holds. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Set categoriser.model back to v1 in deploy/values-production.yaml until a deploy carrying the fix from PR #567 has gone out, so the repository says what should run. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Route CategorisationConfidenceLow alerts on io-shop to the on-call rota so a person is paged. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 13 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 7c3ca00 changed.
- 21 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 3 minutes after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #567.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in while Argus handled it.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Supporting information

Changes to production read
P1 | Nov 11, 2026, 22:05:10 UTC deploy d268103 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
P2 | 02:05:10 UTC deploy 7c3ca00 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory

Log messages read (UTC)
Not read.
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 7c3ca00 to io-shop, compared against d268103 - the revision deployed before it.
modified deploy/values-production.yaml
  @@ -61,4 +61,4 @@ cache:
   # shop loads - so moving to a new model is a change here, reviewed and synced
   # like any other, and moving back is a rollback rather than a rebuild.
   categoriser:
  -  model: v1
  +  model: v2
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | All of this describes main. The deployed revision 7c3ca00 is not in main's history, so I can't confirm its categorising.py matches what I read.

The fault: in src/io_shop/categorising.py, the comment above V2 says its vocabulary was built from titles the training pipeline had already lowercased, and that V2 "takes words exactly as it is given them" (lowercases_its_input=False). The serving path did not match that. categorise passed title.split() straight to predict without lowercasing anything. So under V2, any word in a title that wasn't already lowercase was looked up as-is and missed the lowercase vocabulary. "Kettle in brushed steel" went to "General" with confident=False. V1 never had this problem because it lowercases inside predict. Switching categoriser.model to v2 in deploy/values-production.yaml didn't break anything new. It took away the lowercasing V1 had been doing for the code, so capitalised product words stopped matching. And because a "General" filing is not an error, error rate and latency stayed flat while confidence fell.

The fix: categorise now lowercases the title before splitting it (title.lower().split()), doing the same step the comment says V2's training pipeline did. For V1 nothing changes, since its predict already lowercases every word before lookup. Both versions stay loadable, so the config is safe on v1 or v2. predict and the model definitions are unchanged.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_categorising.py gets a case asserting that V2 files capitalised titles ("Kettle in brushed steel", "KEYBOARD with backlight", "Fitness Smartwatch") confidently and in the right category. Against the old categorise those lookups would miss and return "General", so the new assertions should fail on the old code. The existing V2 tests only used words that were already lowercase, which is why they never caught this. None of this has been run.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | deploy/values-production.yaml at 7c3ca00

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, io-shop stopped confidently sorting some shoppers' purchases into categories. The shop had switched to a newer model for this sorting. That model only knows lowercase words, but the shop passed product titles to it without lowercasing them, which likely left capitalised words in those titles unrecognised. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. To end it, Argus rolled back the io-shop deployment. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off. Argus has also proposed a fix, but it is only open as a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
